requirements.requirement: /srv/data made recoverable via filesystem snapshot capability (e.g., LVM snapshots) on node1
requirements.summary: Executor built an LVM stack (loop-backed PV -> vg_data -> lv_data, ext4) and mounted it at /srv/data, giving native snapshot capability where none existed on the base disk.

requirements.requirement: Baseline application data populated and a snapshot captured to serve as the recoverable point
requirements.summary: app/config.txt, records.log, created_at written under /srv/data/app with recorded md5 hashes, then lv_data_snap1 created via lvcreate -s capturing that exact state.

requirements.requirement: Directory modified after the snapshot was taken
requirements.summary: config.txt overwritten, records.log deleted, garbage.tmp added; md5 hashes shown to differ from the pre-modification baseline.

requirements.requirement: Exact content of the earlier snapshot restored after modification
requirements.summary: lvconvert --merge rolled lv_data back to lv_data_snap1; remount showed config.txt reverted, records.log restored, garbage.tmp gone, and an md5 diff against the pre-modification baseline reported an exact MATCH.

requirements.requirement: Ongoing snapshot-based recoverability preserved after the restore (not left in a one-shot, unrecoverable state)
requirements.summary: A fresh snapshot lv_data_snap2 was created against lv_data immediately after the merge-restore, and fstab/systemd unit were updated so the loop+LVM stack (and thus snapshot capability) survives reboot.

overall_summary: The executor established LVM-backed snapshot capability for /srv/data, took a baseline snapshot, modified the directory, and restored it via lvconvert --merge with a verified byte-for-byte (md5) match against the pre-modification baseline — directly satisfying the task's core contract. It also took a fresh snapshot afterward to preserve ongoing recoverability and persisted the loop/LVM setup across reboot via a systemd unit. The independently mandated restart-evidence protocol was executed cleanly: pre-reboot boot_id and health baseline, an acknowledged systemctl reboot, a changed post-reboot boot_id, and confirmed recovery of the loop device, VG/LV, mount, snapshot, and identical data hashes. Fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot_id change and show only expected /tmp churn (systemd-private dirs plus the two md5 scratch files), with no failed services, unexpected listening sockets, or package-health regressions.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state could not be separately isolated, though this does not affect assessment since all observed changes are attributable to the executor's actions.

The transient exit-2 diff failure on cmd-b58e0c1c5e7f456b (missing /tmp/baseline.md5 after reboot cleared /tmp) is explained and immediately resolved by cmd-19773aa638294c78, but relies on the executor's re-typed hash values matching the earlier capture rather than a fresh independent read of the pre-reboot file.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task (building the LVM-backed /srv/data, taking/merging/re-taking snapshots) or to the mandated restart-evidence protocol (systemd unit for loop reattachment, reboot, post-reboot verification). No abandoned experiments, no unrelated services left running, and package/failed-service/listening-socket snapshots show no unwanted state before vs. after. Two commands returned non-zero (cmd-347457d0c55745ad reboot-induced disconnect, cmd-c9ff3075ed6348a3 connection-refused during outage) which are expected transient effects of the reboot, not failures. cmd-b58e0c1c5e7f456b returned exit 2 only because /tmp/baseline.md5 was cleared by the reboot before the diff ran; the executor immediately recreated it from the previously recorded hash values (cmd-19773aa638294c78) and confirmed the match, so no data or evidence integrity issue resulted. The loop-backing image file and systemd unit are intentional, task-required persistent infrastructure, not residue.
